paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: The figure is a nested (two-ring) donut chart showing the distribution of samples (in percent) across two ambiguity-related metrics, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity Std” categories and the inner ring representing “Max Ambiguity” categories. The outer ring contains 4 slices with percentage labels inside the segments: “Std: 0.0” (dark teal) at approximately 49.0%, “Std: 0.47” (medium teal/blue) at approximately 39.0%, “Std: 0.82” (brighter blue) at approximately 5.0%, and “Std: 0.94” (light cyan) at approximately 7.0%. The inner ring contains 3 slices, also labeled with percentages: “Max: 1” (medium light blue) at approximately 47.7%, “Max: 2” (lighter blue) at approximately 38.0%, and “Max: 3” (very pale blue) at approximately 14.2%. Two separate legends appear on the right—one titled “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” mapping colors to the four standard deviation values, and one titled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” mapping colors to the three maximum ambiguity values—and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized beyond the color coding and internal percentage annotations.
